problem: The velocity $v$ (in $\text{m/s}$) of a particle at time $t$ (in seconds) is given by $v(t)=4{t}^{2}-16t+15.$ Calculate the velocity of the particle when the acceleration $a$ is equal to $0\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

feedback.problem:
The velocity $v$ (in $\text{m/s}$) of a particle at time $t$ (in seconds) is given by $v(t)=\sqrt{{t}^{2}+t+7}.$ Calculate the velocity of the particle when the acceleration $a$ is equal to $\frac{1}{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

When $a=\frac{1}{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2},$ the velocity is $v=$
{{field-1}}
$\text{m/s}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate $v(t)$ to calculate $a(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+t+7}) \\  & =\frac{2t+1}{2\sqrt{{t}^{2}+t+7}}\end{aligned}
$$

To calculate the time when the acceleration is $a=\frac{1}{2},$ we substitute this into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & =\frac{2t+1}{2\sqrt{{t}^{2}+t+7}} \\ 1 & =\frac{2t+1}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+t+7}} \\ \sqrt{{t}^{2}+t+7} & =2t+1 \\ {(\sqrt{{t}^{2}+t+7})}^{2} & ={(2t+1)}^{2} \\ {t}^{2}+t+7 & =4{t}^{2}+4t+1 \\ 0 & =3{t}^{2}+3t-6 \\ 0 & ={t}^{2}+t-2 \\ 0 & =(t-1)(t+2) \\ t & =1,\,-2\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $t=1$ since $t\ge 0.$

Then, to calculate the velocity at time $t=1,$ we substitute this into the equation for the velocity:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1) & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+1+7} \\  & =\sqrt{1+1+7} \\  & =3\text{ m/s}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity when $a=\frac{1}{2}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}$ is $v=3\,\text{m/s}.$
